title: Buck out of jail and Bubbles picking tomatoes
summary: Buck served about six months and went back to his old friends, while Bubbles refused a pay cut and sorted tomatoes.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: This isn't the period when Buck was in jail?

No, no, wait. Buck was out. I told you about him coming out, told you about getting a cab, I told you about that -- about his getting a cab, you don't remember that? Yes, I told you about his getting a cab and he let me know he was getting out and I was going to meet him -- I didn't tell you that? Well, let me tell you. He stayed -- I think he had six months and he got out. He didn't tell me he was getting out or I would have come and met him or come after him or something. But he didn't tell me -- he just got out and went on home. Then he called me when he got home. Then I'm going to his house to see him and in the meantime I'm going to tell him about not telling anybody he's out and to not hang out with none of the fellows he was hanging out with before. That was just like talking to water on a duck's back, pouring water on a duck's

back. Pour water on a duck's back. So he says, I got a cab and it came over -- I'm going to talk to my friends, he was going to do so-and-so. He was going to do the same like he did. Sure 'nuff. Really? Yeah, he said, okay.
That's what you're going to do now? You don't realize what I've gone through in getting a job, instead of picking tomatoes that I told you about.
That's what you were doing while he was in jail?
That's right, I was picking tomatoes because I wouldn't take a cut in salary -- you know.
Then I got the job as I told you in a speakeasy, a little cafe on 47th Street or 46th Street.
